raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #45317

## Motivation

The forward hooks page says hooks are attached in `ModelRunner.initialize` and "run on every forward pass". That's not what happens. Hooks are registered **after** CUDA graph capture (`finalize_cuda_graph_capture`), and CUDA graph replay never runs Python hooks. With default settings on CUDA, decode and prefill both use CUDA graphs, so a hook can silently never run.

In #45317, a hook on `model.layers.14` of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (v0.5.21, NVIDIA L4) ran **0 times** for a 128-token request with default settings. It ran **128 times** with CUDA graphs disabled.

## Modifications

Docs only: `docs/docs/advanced_features/forward_hooks.mdx`.

- Fix the intro line: hooks are attached after CUDA graph capture and don't run on graph replay.
- "Hook lifecycle": replace the old `ModelRunner.initialize()` snippet with the real registration code from `finalize_cuda_graph_capture`.
- Key points: say hooks run only on the eager path.
- New section **"Hooks and CUDA graphs"**: why hooks don't run, and how to make them run on every step (`--disable-decode-cuda-graph --disable-prefill-cuda-graph`, or the engine kwargs `disable_decode_cuda_graph=True, disable_prefill_cuda_graph=True`). It also notes that this lowers throughput.
- Summary: same correction.

No code changes. A startup warning when `forward_hooks` are set while CUDA graphs are on could be a follow-up PR.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable (docs only).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable (docs only). For context, #45317 has the throughput cost of disabling CUDA graphs on an L4.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`pre-commit run --files docs/docs/advanced_features/forward_hooks.mdx` passes.)
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Not applicable, docs only.)
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable, docs only.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Note: the measurement in #45317 used `disable_cuda_graph=True` on v0.5.21. The per-phase flags in this doc (`--disable-decode-cuda-graph`, `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph`) are the current ones on `main`, but I haven't re-run the measurement with them.

 * Debugging model internals
 * Exporting hidden states to external tooling
 
-Hooks are attached once during `ModelRunner.initialize` and run on every forward pass.
+Hooks are attached once at startup, after CUDA graph capture. They run on every forward pass that runs in eager mode, but **not** when a captured CUDA graph is replayed. With default settings on CUDA, both decode and prefill use CUDA graphs, so a hook may never run. See [Hooks and CUDA graphs](#hooks-and-cuda-graphs).
 
 ***
 ### Configuration overview
@@ -149,11 +149,15 @@ The first two cause initialization to fail fast with a descriptive error; the la
 ***
 ### Hook lifecycle and behavior
 
-Hooks are registered in `ModelRunner.initialize()`:
+Hooks are registered once at startup, right after CUDA graph capture (`finalize_cuda_graph_capture` in `model_runner_components/cuda_graph_setup.py`):
 
 ```python Example
-if server_args.forward_hooks:
-    register_forward_hooks(self.model, server_args.forward_hooks)
+# Register forward hooks AFTER cuda-graph capture so their tensor ops are
+# not traced into any captured graph — capture stays hook-free and hooks
+# fire only on the eager forward path (capture replay never runs Python
+# hooks anyway).
+if get_observability().forward_hooks:
+    register_forward_hooks(model_runner.model, get_observability().forward_hooks)
 ```
 
 The actual registration logic is implemented by `register_forward_hooks`:
@@ -218,11 +222,42 @@ def register_forward_hooks(model: nn.Module, hook_specs: List[dict[str, Any]]) -
 Key points:
 
 * Hooks are **forward hooks only** (via `module.register_forward_hook`).
-* They are attached once at initialization.
+* They are attached once at startup, after CUDA graph capture.
+* They run only on the eager forward path. They do **not** run when a CUDA graph is replayed (see below).
 * Hook handles are currently not stored on `ModelRunner` (they cannot be removed later via this API).
 * Failure to match any modules is non-fatal; a warning is logged instead.
 * If a hook factory returns `None`, a warning is logged and that spec is skipped.
 
+***
+### Hooks and CUDA graphs
+
+A CUDA graph replay runs the captured GPU kernels directly and does not call into Python, so PyTorch forward hooks do not run on replayed steps. SGLang registers hooks after graph capture so that the captured graphs stay hook-free.
+
+With default settings on CUDA, both the decode phase and the prefill phase use CUDA graphs. A hook then runs only on batches that fall back to the eager path, which may be never. No warning is logged.
+
+To make hooks run on every forward pass, disable CUDA graphs for both phases:
+
+```bash Command
+python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <model> \
+  --disable-decode-cuda-graph --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \
+  --forward-hooks '[{"name": "...", "target_modules": ["..."], "hook_factory": "my_project.hooks:factory"}]'
+```
+
+With the offline engine:
+
+```python Example
+import sglang as sgl
+
+llm = sgl.Engine(
+    model_path="<model>",
+    forward_hooks=[...],
+    disable_decode_cuda_graph=True,
+    disable_prefill_cuda_graph=True,
+)
+```
+
+`--cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled` does the same. Disabling CUDA graphs lowers throughput; how much depends on the GPU, the model and the batch size.
+
 ***
 ### Writing a hook factory
